history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration consider the actual deployment and the revised role of the videoconferencing team when updating the agreements with the United Nations Office for Project Services.
history.administration_response: The revised role of the video conferencing team has been incorporated into the updated financial agreement with UNOPS under the virtual events management cluster. The financial agreement outlines the objectives, activities, scope and expected deliverables for virtual events management which cover UniteVC, Teams Live, WebEx and Zoom. The updated financial agreement (OICT FA 02 – OSD) has been provided for reference. The Office of Information and Communications Technology requests the closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the financial agreement with UNOPS was revised in 2024, the Board will need further time and information to make ensure that this revised financial agreement actually improves the resource utilization and enhances cost effectiveness. The Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: In paragraph 109 of its report, the Board recommended that the Administration consider the actual deployment and the revised role of the videoconferencing team when updating the agreements with UNOPS.
history.reference_raw: Report of the Board for the year ended 31 December 2022 8
history.entities_raw: Office of Information and Communications Technology
history.sg_progress: The Office of Information and Communications Technology revised its financial agreement with UNOPS and included the following language to reflect the virtual events management service: “UNGSC Virtual Events Management Service support from Brindisi and Valencia to the Secretariat locations and other external clients”. The United Nations Secretariat conducts meetings and events on premises, virtually and in hybrid mode (a mix of virtual and in-person components). The virtual events management team will deliver high-quality virtual and hybrid events by ensuring seamless technical execution, including event support, audiovisual production, live multi-language streaming and platform integration. With scattered technology platforms in use throughout the United Nations and multiple end-user devices (personal and in meeting spaces), the virtual events management team will focus on optimizing efficiency and cost effectiveness by streamlining event production processes to maximize efficiency and minimize costs, and leverage technology and automation to streamline event setup, operation and management. The virtual events management team will explore opportunities to repurpose resources across multiple events and continuously evaluate and optimize the use of resources to ensure cost effectiveness. Updated with the most recent trends, technologies and best practices in virtual and hybrid events, the virtual events management team will continuously evaluate and enhance virtual and hybrid event strategies on the basis of feedback and analytics. Working alongside the Global Engineering and Conferencing Section, the team will advocate for innovation and experimentation to drive continuous improvement and encourage collaboration and knowledge-sharing within the United Nations global conferencing community. The United Nations owns on-premise conferencing and collaboration infrastructure for high-level, high-visibility events spanning four geographical locations, which requires technical infrastructure management and support. The virtual events management team will ensure that this infrastructure is robust and reliable. The team will also explore new technologies and techniques that can be added or to complement existing infrastructure to improve the quality of virtual and hybrid events and to lower costs.
